column1: # library/ began as a byte-identical copy of the bootstrap's library at v0.0.162 (7ba8bd1d). The
# reference compiler is always run against ITS OWN library (SYSL_ORACLE_LIB, or the one installed
# beside it) and this compiler against this one, so after a change here the two compile against
# **The rule for an oracle sweep**: it may differ from the reference only in what reaches a module
# listed here. A sweep's disagreement is green when every disagreeing block, or every disagreeing
# symbol, reaches a listed module; anything else is a defect. With no rows the two libraries are the
# same bytes and every sweep must answer exactly as it does against the reference's library.

column3: new module, not in the reference's library: skip(why) -> never ends a test without a verdict (\u{3}, the reason, exit 0); outside the root module so it cannot collide with sysl.harness.skip

spare slots hold no value: storage is slot_storage, grow/push/extend/buf_with_capacity slot_place, pop/truncate/clear/remove slot_vacate; Buf is a reference handle over a boxed BufCore (assignment, parameter, capture and containment share one buffer; no zero value; elems a read-only property; copy() makes a second buffer); impl IndexSet takes self (a copy of the handle writes the one container), so b[i] = x works on a val; impl Walk for Buf[T] (Walker = []T, walk = view()), so for x in b walks the view

six tests: set, pop, truncate/clear and remove let go at once; growth adds no count; buf_with_capacity keeps no fill; the invariant tests write a BufCore; ten share tests and two copy() tests; the zero-buffer test moved to the compiler (tests_brf_buf_reference.sysl); two for tests: a buffer walked directly (empty too), and one grown during the walk walked as it was

slots are Option[T] filled with None, so a vacated slot owns nothing; Deque.elems and DequeCursor.elems private; Deque is a reference handle over a shared &DequeCore[T] (ring, head, count; head/count read-only properties), so every copy names one deque and deque() allocates; impl IndexSet takes self (a copy of the handle writes the one container), so b[i] = x works on a val; walk moved into impl Walk for Deque[T], so for x in d walks its cursor

two tests: pop_front/pop_back let go of what they take out; clear lets go of every element and keeps no fill. Seven share tests: assignment (push_front through the copy), parameter, closure capture, nested deque, copied struct, growth through the other name, destructor waits for the last name; two for tests: walked front to back (empty too), and grown during the walk walked as it was

a child is started with posix_spawnp (macOS, glibc >= 2.29), not fork + execvp: fork cost grew with the parent heap (20 ms a test in a runner that had just compiled slate); the named variables are merged into the envp in the parent, and a PATH among them is searched as execvp searched it
one test: a variable named twice reaches the child once, with the second value

new module, not in the reference's library: Rational over BigInt in lowest terms (denominator positive, zero denominator traps, checked_of answers None), + - * / and negation, Eq/Ord/Hash, floor/ceil/trunc, n/d Display
new module file: from_real (exact), cmp_real/eq_real/lt_real/gt_real at the double's exact value (NaN unordered), to_real correctly rounded ties-to-even, subnormals included

30 tests: canonical form, checked_of, From (a bare literal reaching From[long] among two implementations), arithmetic, order, hashing, floor/ceil/trunc, exact real comparison, to_real ties, near-ties, subnormals and overflow
one test: BigInt.from(3) reaches From[long] rather than From[u64] (a bare integer literal prefers the signed widening)

Map is a reference: a one-field handle over &MapCore[K, V], which carries the table and both counts (a copy used to share the table and keep its own counts); every public method keeps its signature and delegates; cell/count/dead are read-only properties; map() allocates the core and still no table; walk moved into impl Walk for Map[K, V], so for (k, v) in m walks its cursor; copy walks self

ten tests: a put/grow/remove/clear through a second name, a by-value parameter, a closure capture, a map read out of a map, a copied holder struct and a walk all share; values are let go when the last name dies, and at the call on replace/remove; one for test: entries walked as (k, v) pairs (empty too)
three tests: a Set shares through its Map (a second name, a by-value parameter, growth); one for test: keys walked directly (empty too)
two tests, ignored until Buf is a handle: a Heap shares through its Buf (a second name, a by-value parameter)

add, remove and clear take the Set by value: a val-bound set is added to, the handle copy sharing the one map; walk moved into impl Walk for Set[K], so for k in s walks its cursor; union/intersection/difference/is_subset walk the sets directly
push, pop and clear take the Heap by value: a val-bound heap is pushed into, the handle copy sharing the one Buf

new module, not in the reference's library: format_count(i128) -> int (a count saturated at int) and format_spec_of(width, prec, left) -> FormatSpec (C's reading of a negative count), which the compiler calls for an f"..." specifier whose width or precision is a hole
five tests: a count in range, saturation both ways, a negative width left-justifies, a negative precision is absent, the flag still left-justifies
new trait Walk (type Walker; walk(self) -> Self::Walker): what a for walks a container through, the compiler calling walk() once before the first turn
walk moved into impl Walk for List[T], so for x in l walks its cursor
doc comment only: the resolve loop walks the Buf directly (for a in resolve(...)?)
two loops walk the resolved Buf directly rather than its view()
one loop walks self.line directly rather than its view()
one loop walks a Buf[string] directly rather than its view()
walk moved into impl Walk for Ring[T], so for x in r walks its cursor
one test: for walks a ring front to back, an empty one not at all
one test: for walks a list from its head, an empty one not at all

to_upper and to_title answer ß (U+00DF) for ß, as UnicodeData.txt 17.0.0 has no simple uppercase or titlecase for it; utf8proc 2.11.0 answered ẞ (U+1E9E). Every other code point was checked against the database and agrees

the sharp-s test now asserts to_upper/to_title(ß) == ß and is_lower(ß); three tests: asymmetric pairs (Kelvin, Ohm, Angstrom, long s, final sigma, dotted/dotless i), Cherokee and Georgian, the titlecase digraphs
states the ß correction and the UnicodeData.txt comparison (URL, SHA-256)
to_upper("straße") == "STRAßE", to_lower("STRAẞE") == "straße"
doc comment only: ß has no simple uppercase
doc comment only: the sharp-s example is ẞ lower-casing to ß
